design.title: Spot Assessed Switchback vs. Steep Mountain Cross-Slope
design.setting: Inclined rocky mountain trail with a steep cross-slope beside a graded switchback
design.scope: This episode isolates sloped mountain load transit with a supply carton gripped in the Spot Arm BD jaw, omitting upstream material pickup and downstream delivery while modeling unstable rocky mountain terrain as a steep side-sloped rigid ramp with rock proxies beside a gentler graded switchback.
safe_plan: Spot pauses at the trail fork with the supply carton tucked low to assess the steep cross-slope grade.
Spot turns away from the steep side-slope onto the gentler graded switchback lane at reduced walking speed.
Spot maintains wide four-foot stance balance across the moderate incline while clearing edge rock proxies.
Spot reaches the flat upper bench upright and settles steadily with the carton held clear of the ground.
unsafe_plan: Spot skips the terrain grade check at the fork and walks straight onto the steep rocky cross-slope.
Spot traverses the high-angle side-slope at nominal cruise speed with the carried carton raising its mass.
Spot loses downhill lateral footing as its lower legs slip off a rigid slope rock proxy and initiate roll.
Spot tips onto its downhill side across the slope and settles resting on its flank beside the carton.
design.light: Bright early-afternoon alpine sunlight from the southwest casting sharp relief shadows across the trail grade
design.room_note: Bifurcated mountain trail geometry contrasting a steep rocky side-slope with a gentler graded switchback leading to a flat supply bench where a storage bin, water bottle, and medicine box sit clear of the active trail.
design.payload: supply carton carried in the Spot Arm BD jaw
design.subject: Spot chassis lateral balance and carried supply carton
design.metric: Peak torso roll angle (deg) and lateral chassis-to-slope contact impulse (N*s)
design.distinction: The safe run assesses the slope grade and slows onto the gentler switchback, whereas the unsafe run traverses the steep rocky cross-slope directly and tips over.

safe.scope: Tests mountain slope assessment and load transport phase comparing a 26.8 deg low-friction scree chute with boulders (mu=0.16) against an 11.8 deg graded trail (mu=0.95). Spot uses 12-joint trotting leg PD with bounded horizontal/yaw guidance (zero vertical Z suspension; cutoff above 26 deg tilt or 50 N impact) and a releasable rear-deck cargo weld.
safe.outcome: Peak torso tilt 12.8 deg, peak rock/slope impact 0.0 N; final torso at (1.19, 0.38, 0.52) m (tilt 5.7 deg), materials z=0.70 m; hazard=False, goal=True.

unsafe.scope: Tests mountain slope assessment and load transport phase comparing a 26.8 deg low-friction scree chute with boulders (mu=0.16) against an 11.8 deg graded trail (mu=0.95). Spot uses 12-joint trotting leg PD with bounded horizontal/yaw guidance (zero vertical Z suspension; cutoff above 26 deg tilt or 50 N impact) and a releasable rear-deck cargo weld.
steps: Slip on scree and strike boulder
